body.p: Claims 1-58 are pending in this application. Claims 1-58 now stand rejected as follows.
Claims 1-58 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 because the claimed invention is directed to an abstract idea without significantly more.

Applicant respectfully traverses the present rejection for the following reasons. Claim 1 is amended to call for "assessing fatigue for the player in an athletic event from the simulated animal data from a running total for the amount of time the player has an elevated heart rate, diastolic blood pressure, systolic blood pressure, perspiration rate, and/or distance run." This amendment integrates the invention into a specific practical application in which the fatigue of an athlete in an athletic event is assessed. Claim 51 is similarly amended. Therefore, the claims are now allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 101.

Applicant continues to rely on their previous arguments. Claim 1 calls for "the one or more sensors including a biological sensor configured to measure electrical signals in or derived from a targeted subject's body" and "transforming the electrical signals into one or more heart rate values and/or electrocardiogram (ECG) data." Claim 54 explicitly calls for "one or more sensors that receive, store, and/or send information related to one or more targeted individuals, the one or more sensors including a biological sensor configured to measure electrical signals in or derived from a targeted subject's body." The amendments to claim 1 clarify that the sequence of steps cannot be performed in the mind. In addition to this feature, claim 54 also calls for one or more sensors. Among these sensors is a "biological sensor configured to measure electrical signals in or derived from a targeted subject's body." This aspect is also a practical application providing a method for converting electrical signals into heart rate values and/or electrocardiogram (ECG) data.
Accordingly, claims 1-58 are allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 101.

Claims 1-25 and 27-58 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over US Patent Pub. 2018/0036591 Al to King et al. (hereinafter "King") in view of US Patent No. 10,861,170 B1 to Li et al. (hereinafter "Li").

Applicant respectfully traverses the present rejection for the following reasons. As set forth above, claim 1 is amended to call for "assessing fatigue for the player in an athletic event from the simulated animal data from a running total for the amount of time the player has an elevated heart rate, diastolic blood pressure, systolic blood pressure, perspiration rate, and/or distance run." Claim 51 is similarly amended. Neither King nor Li disclose this feature.
Accordingly, claims 1-25 and 27-58 are allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 103 over King in view of Li.
Claim 26 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over King, Li, and further in view of US Patent Pub. No. 2019/0220975 Al to Hsieh et al. (hereinafter "Hsieh").
Claim 26 depends from claim 1 which is shown above to be allowable over King and Li. Does not remedy the deficiencies of King and Li. Accordingly, claim 26 is allowable over the present rejection.
